A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MATT task, MisEngine data construction, and MisFormer model. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains readable supplementary Sections A–E, included in this assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original attribution and mistake-detection experiments on EPIC-KITCHENS-M, Ego4D-M, and EgoPER, including model comparisons and ablations in Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original human-study results, SRL evaluation, zero-shot transfer, a semantic-head ablation, and additional analyses in its supplement.

M1.justification: MisEngine's construction procedure and MisFormer's architecture, losses, attention mechanisms, and inference gating are unchanged. Appendix A elaborates existing matching rules; removing the semantic head is an additional ablation, not a revision of the proposed model.

E1.justification: Appendix B newly uses CaptainCook4D in a four-dataset human realism evaluation and adds human assessment of inherited annotations. The principal model benchmarks and attribution tasks remain unchanged. Zero-shot EgoPER evaluation changes the protocol on retained coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–5 retain the same semantic, temporal, spatial, and detection comparators, including ChatGPT, EgoT2, SSDA, AMNAR, and EgoPED. The supplementary experiments introduce no additional competing model; added citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendices A–C add distinct evaluation protocols: SRL assessment on 1,000 Ego4D descriptions, a 16-participant realism study using 200 text-video pairs per dataset and a Real-% metric, and zero-shot EgoPER testing. Existing benchmark splits and metrics remain unchanged; newly disclosed training settings do not establish a changed training protocol.

E4.justification: The supplement substantially expands validation and diagnosis through sample and annotation realism assessment, SRL reliability testing, zero-shot transfer, spatial performance by mistake type, and an ablation removing the semantic head. Figure 5 adds success and temporal-failure cases. The original Table 6 ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B introduces mean-plus/minus variability reporting for human realism ratings, with the discussion identifying standard deviation. v1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. The aggregation underlying these deviations is not fully specified, and model-benchmark seed or repeated-run reporting is not added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain identical values. New results include predicate/object SRL F1 of 97.97%/94.13%, sample realism of 92.32%/92.42% for the constructed datasets, inherited-annotation realism above 95%, and zero-shot EgoPER scores of 34.46 F1/35.52 accuracy. The semantic-head ablation reports 0.358 s MAE and 65.33% mIoU; mistake-type breakdowns and qualitative findings are also added. These are additional evaluations, not improvements to retained same-setting results.

T1.justification: The formal MATT outputs, dataset-construction equations, and loss definitions are unchanged. The supplement adds no substantive mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations; its matching-rule discussion elaborates the existing formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract newly claims that human evaluation establishes ecological validity and reliable benchmarking. It also replaces general outperformance wording with explicit minimum margins of 6.66%, 21.81%, 18.7%, and 3.00%. The central MATT, MisEngine, and MisFormer contributions and conclusion otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendices B–D add substantive interpretations of dataset realism, explain compact union boxes through hand-object overlap, diagnose tension between semantic and grounded representations, and attribute a temporal failure to ambiguity in 2D completion cues. Appendix C also newly describes Table 6(e) as removing spatial supervision, although the retained main-text experiment replaces attention heatmaps with GradCAM.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and discloses AdamW, learning rate 10^-4, 20 epochs, four H100 GPUs, and batch size 64 in Appendix E. These training details were absent from v1; their disclosure does not demonstrate that the underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: Seven cited works are added, mainly through a brief instructional-AI discussion, including Towards effective human-in-the-loop assistive AI agents and Transparent and coherent procedural mistake detection. Existing references and the principal positioning against earlier mistake-understanding work are retained.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, makes limited wording changes, adds an acknowledgement, and organizes new supplementary material into Sections A–E. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact; this is not extensive rewriting or restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds three supplementary table panels and Figure 5. Existing Figures 1–4 and table structures retain their content, with limited reflow: Table 1 changes columns on page 5, and Table 4 moves from page 7 to page 8.

improvement.justification: The human validation supplies evidence missing from v1 for the constructed datasets, while the new ablation, failure analysis, and training configuration improve transparency and diagnostic value. The gain is limited by brief study documentation and reporting inconsistencies: Appendix C mischaracterizes the GradCAM ablation, and the abstract's quantified spatial-superiority claim is not supported against SSDA in unchanged Table 4. The additions nevertheless provide a useful net improvement.
